lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: EXPERIENCE appears after EDUCATION, though the engineering roles establish the career direction more directly.
items.because: A recruiter may reach the degrees before the strongest evidence of engineering work.

items.says: The résumé includes a date of birth and nationality, personal details conventionally left off.
items.because: Readers are not meant to weigh them when assessing qualifications, and they draw attention from role-relevant information.

items.says: The 35% accuracy improvement lacks a comparison baseline and evaluation set.
items.because: Readers cannot tell how the change was measured or whether it is relative or percentage-point.

items.says: “Their” makes it unclear whose signal scope the routing layer enforces.
items.because: The phrase refers to both the specialist agents and the independent reviewer.

items.says: The tool-call and latency reductions come after the rollout and reward details.
items.because: That buries the clearest evidence of impact for a scanning reader.

items.says: This bullet repeats the adapter fine-tuning work in the earlier bullet.
items.because: Both mention assistant-only loss masking, and this bullet adds no distinct result.

items.says: Two entries give conflicting reductions for the same triage achievement.
items.because: This bullet reports 68%, while the research-agent project reports two-thirds for the same triage branch and signals per case.

items.says: The claim that switching from FP32 to BF16 cut GPU memory by 4x overstates what that change alone typically achieves.
items.because: Converted tensors take roughly half the space, while other fine-tuning memory may remain in FP32.

items.says: The repeated “by” makes the reduction and its method clunky to read.
items.because: Readers must work through the repeated construction before reaching the precision change.

items.says: The load-test threshold does not establish the exact p95 value of 180 ms.
items.because: A passing test establishes only that p95 is at most 200 ms.

items.says: “Maintained” and “adds” mix past and present tense in an ended role.
items.because: The shift can look like an editing oversight.

items.says: The line attributes the three-day release cycle to the regression checks without showing they caused it.
items.because: Automated checks do not necessarily determine the duration of the full release cycle.

items.says: The three-day release cycle lacks a previous duration for comparison.
items.because: Readers cannot tell how large the improvement was.

items.says: “Automated regression checks” does not say what the checks cover.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what failure modes or model behavior they guard against.

items.says: The line credits the event-queue migration with eliminating nightly backlogs without establishing causation.
items.because: Queues, retries and dead-letter handling do not guarantee that backlogs disappear.

items.says: The backlog and dispatch outcome has no before-and-after measure.
items.because: The count of services shows scale, not how much the backlog or dispatch delay changed.

items.says: “AI-first engineering practices” does not specify what was introduced or changed.
items.because: Readers cannot picture the contribution or tell what the teams adopted.

items.says: “Accelerating delivery and improving outcomes” gives no specific result or evidence.
items.because: Readers cannot assess the benefits without knowing what changed or what the comparison was.

items.says: The context limit does not lead the bullet as the main result.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the under-10K-token limit.

items.says: The changes do not by themselves establish that all deadlocks and lost tool results were eliminated.
items.because: Other cyclic waits can still deadlock, and completion-gated writes do not ensure results are durably stored and correctly correlated.

items.says: The 50-way fan-out load does not show how consistently failures were eliminated.
items.because: The load condition shows scale, not evidence that the fix worked reliably.

items.says: The failure outcome appears after the implementation details.
items.because: That makes the result harder to spot when scanning.

items.says: The metrics-integration bullet gives no outcome beyond the integration itself.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what it enabled or improved for the framework or its users.

items.says: The Kendall correlation does not identify the two rankings or values it compares.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what the result validates or interpret its relevance.

items.says: “Showed the evaluator tracks” is awkward wording.
items.because: The unnatural construction makes the degradation result harder to parse.

items.says: The backlog-triage bullet repeats the internship result and does not fit the evaluation-framework project.
items.because: The project's other bullets concern evaluation, so the repeated triage result has unclear attribution and may look like double credit.
